successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: the Lakhmid land at al-Hira and in north-eastern Arabia, annexed when Khosrow II deposed al-Nu'man III in 602 (the 990 cells of Cliopatria's Lakhmid shape that the Sasanian shape of 602 adds)

ledger.x: 270: the Lakhmid kingdom rises at al-Hira as a client of the Sasanian Empire.
270: the Lakhmids are a Sasanian client state.
521: the Himyarites move against the Lakhmids in Najd.
602: Khosrow II deposes al-Nu'man III and annexes the kingdom.

wars.name: Himyarite campaign against the Lakhmids in Najd
wars.outcome: The Himyarites, answering appeals from local Arab tribes, forced the Lakhmids to withdraw from Najd.

wars.name: Lakhmid raids on Roman Syria in the Iberian War
wars.outcome: Al-Mundhir III ravaged Syria in 526 and 528 (capturing two Roman commanders in 526) and in 529 took the Khabour frontier area and marched towards Nisibis, Apamea and Chalcedon but could not take Antioch; no border moved.

wars.name: Lakhmid-Ghassanid wars
wars.outcome: Al-Mundhir III 'defeated the Ghassanids at the famous Battle of Callinicum in 531 AD' (Lakhmid page) and was killed fighting al-Harith ibn Jabalah's Ghassanids at Yawm Halima in June 554 (Mundhir III page).

wars.name: Deposition of al-Nu'man III and the Battle of Dhi Qar
wars.outcome: Khosrow II seized al-Nu'man III at Ctesiphon in 602 and ended the kingdom; the Banu Bakr then beat a Persian force with Arab auxiliaries under Iyas ibn Qabisah at Dhi Qar in southern Iraq ('between 604 and 611 AD'; Muslim traditions 602-624), 'may have been…

certainty.note: The desert frontier with the Ghassanids and Rome and the southern limit in Arabia are approximate throughout; the Euphrates side at al-Hira is the only fixed edge and no treaty line is recorded on the pages opened.
